key_insight: Quantum data reuploading expands a QNN’s accessible Fourier frequencies in a precise lattice-governed way: directions saturate early, but the spectrum keeps growing with reuploads, increasing model capacity.
engineering_relevance: This gives a concrete design rule for quantum models: more reuploads increase expressivity and capacity, but also raise complexity and sensitivity to encoding choices.
method: Characterized the QDR frequency set as an integer-lattice word-length condition: K_R = {k in L : ℓ_T(k) ≤ R}.
Proved that the span of accessible directions stabilizes at R = 1, while the number of frequencies grows polynomially with R.
Derived a Rademacher-complexity bound scaling like √(|K_R|/n) to connect spectrum size with learnability.
evidence_signal: Simulations matched the Fourier-spectrum theory exactly, and benchmark tests showed the QDR can beat a matched MLP on some smooth/periodic univariate tasks and the spiral task, but not on harder multivariate regression.
watch_item: Performance is highly sensitive to the input-encoding scale in multivariate settings, so tuning the encoding map is a critical implementation risk.
paper_title: On the Expressive Power and Capacity of Quantum Data Reuploaders
